candidates.tagline: The $895 camera that turns your phone back into a camera
candidates.story: Huawei launched the Ruiying Z10 on October 1, 2026 — a $895, 346g camera module with a 1-inch sensor and 10x optical zoom that screws onto the Mate 90 Pro Max via a DSLR-style bayonet mount. The entire premise of smartphone photography was eliminating the need to carry a separate camera; the Z10 reverses that by bolting a lens bigger than many mirrorless bodies onto a phone.
candidates.why_funny: The phone camera was supposed to replace your camera bag; Huawei's answer to 'how do we improve phone cameras?' is to turn your phone into a camera bag.
candidates.alt: Huawei Mate 90 Pro Max with the Ruiying Z10 camera module screwed onto its back, the large zoom lens barrel extending far beyond the phone's slim profile

candidates.tagline: OpenAI's $100/month AI agents look like Tamagotchis — and the demo froze
candidates.story: On September 29, 2026, OpenAI unveiled 'Dots' at DevDay — always-on AI agents shaped like a cloud with a beret, a frog, a heart, and a triangle with glasses, priced at $100/month — but the flagship demo saw the agent 'Dottie' freeze completely for ten seconds when asked to summarise user testing, finally replying only that it was 'still checking.'
candidates.why_funny: OpenAI spent years marketing AI as the future of productivity, then unveiled its always-on personal assistant as a collection of cute plush blob mascots that couldn't respond during their own debut.
candidates.alt: Four colorful OpenAI Dots mascots: a blue cloud with a beret, a green frog, a yellow triangle wearing glasses, and a pink heart wearing sunglasses — the always-on AI agents compared by reviewers to 1990s Tamagotchi toys
